column4: On press, enter the keyboard bootloader to flash firmware. Normal typing stops until the keyboard restarts.
On press, restart the keyboard firmware without entering the bootloader or clearing saved configuration. Held keys are released during restart.

On press, reinitialize the keyboard EEPROM, resetting persistent settings. This can erase saved keymap configuration depending on the firmware, and normally restarts the keyboard. This is a settings reset, not firmware flashing.
Swap Caps Lock and left Ctrl in the keyboard firmware.
Restore the normal mapping of Caps Lock and left Ctrl.
Swap left Ctrl and left Gui in the keyboard firmware.
Restore the normal mapping of left Ctrl and left Gui.
Swap right Ctrl and right Gui in the keyboard firmware.
Restore the normal mapping of right Ctrl and right Gui.
Swap Ctrl and Gui on both sides in the keyboard firmware.
Restore the normal mapping of Ctrl and Gui on both sides.
Toggle the left Ctrl/Gui swap and set the right Ctrl/Gui swap to the same new state.
Swap left Alt and left Gui in the keyboard firmware.
Restore the normal mapping of left Alt and left Gui.
Swap right Alt and right Gui in the keyboard firmware.
Restore the normal mapping of right Alt and right Gui.
Swap Alt and Gui on both sides in the keyboard firmware.
Restore the normal mapping of Alt and Gui on both sides.

Swap Grave and Escape in the keyboard firmware.

Restore the normal mapping of Backslash and Backspace.
Make Caps Lock act as Ctrl in the keyboard firmware.
Stop treating Caps Lock as Ctrl.
Disable the Gui keys. Gui is Command on macOS and Windows or Super on other systems.
Enable the Gui keys. Gui is Command on macOS and Windows or Super on other systems.
Toggle whether the keyboard sends the Gui keys.
Enable N-key rollover when supported by the keyboard and host. N-key rollover lets the keyboard report more simultaneous keys than the usual six-key report; support depends on the keyboard and host.
Disable N-key rollover. N-key rollover lets the keyboard report more simultaneous keys than the usual six-key report; support depends on the keyboard and host.
Toggle N-key rollover when supported by the keyboard and host. N-key rollover lets the keyboard report more simultaneous keys than the usual six-key report; support depends on the keyboard and host.
Save this split keyboard half as the left half. Requires firmware configured for EE_HANDS.
Save this split keyboard half as the right half. Requires firmware configured for EE_HANDS.
Enable the keyboard's sound output. Configured tones, click sounds and an active music mode can be heard; this does not itself enter music mode.
Disable the keyboard's sound output, including configured tones, click sounds and music-mode notes. This does not mute the computer's audio.
Toggle the keyboard's sound output between enabled and disabled. This does not itself enter music mode.
Enable music mode, where keyboard keys play musical notes. Requires audio support.
Disable music mode, where keyboard keys play musical notes. Requires audio support.
Toggle music mode, where keyboard keys play musical notes. Requires audio support.
Cycle the keyboard music mode through its configured scales.
Toggle generated click sounds on each keypress. Requires keyboard audio support.
Raise the pitch of generated keyboard click sounds.
Lower the pitch of generated keyboard click sounds.
Restore the default pitch of generated keyboard click sounds.
Enable haptic feedback when supported by the keyboard.
Disable keyboard haptic feedback.
Toggle keyboard haptic feedback.
Restore the firmware defaults for haptic feedback and enable haptics. This resets vibration settings, not the keyboard layout or all EEPROM settings.
Cycle haptic feedback between keypress, key release, and both.
Toggle solenoid buzz. Requires a solenoid haptic driver.
Select the next vibration pattern. Requires a DRV2605L haptic driver.
Select the previous vibration pattern. Requires a DRV2605L haptic driver.
Toggle continuous vibration on or off instead of short key-triggered pulses. Requires a driver that implements continuous haptic output.
Increase continuous haptic strength. Requires a DRV2605L driver.
Decrease continuous haptic strength. Requires a DRV2605L driver.
Increase solenoid activation time. Requires a solenoid haptic driver.
Decrease solenoid activation time. Requires a solenoid haptic driver.
Reduce the Auto Shift hold timeout by 5 milliseconds, so a supported key becomes shifted sooner.
Increase the Auto Shift hold timeout by 5 milliseconds, so a supported key must be held longer to become shifted.
Type the current Auto Shift timeout in milliseconds into the focused application. Use a text field to read it; this sends text to the host.
Enable Auto Shift: tap a supported key for its normal form, or hold past the timeout for its shifted form. Supported keys and repeat behavior depend on firmware configuration.
Disable Auto Shift, so it no longer adds Shift to keys held past its timeout. Ordinary Shift keys still work.
Toggle Auto Shift: supported keys send their normal form on a tap and their shifted form after a hold past the timeout. Supported keys and repeat behavior depend on firmware configuration.
Enable configured chord processing in the keyboard firmware.
Disable configured chord processing in the keyboard firmware.
Toggle configured chord processing in the keyboard firmware.

On press, toggle Caps Word. While enabled it automatically shifts letters and selected punctuation until a word-breaking key is pressed. Continuing keys and optional idle timeout depend on firmware settings. This does not toggle host Caps Lock or save a persistent state. Requires firmware Caps Word support.

Press to send the last remembered key again with its remembered modifiers; release to release that repeated key. Holding can use normal host key repeat where applicable. Standalone modifiers and layer switches are normally not remembered; if no key is remembered, this sends nothing. Firmware can customize which keys and modifiers are remembered. Requires Repeat Key support.

Press to send the alternate of the last remembered key with its remembered modifiers; release to release it. Defaults include paired opposites such as Left/Right, but firmware and Vial alternate-repeat settings decide the mapping. If no alternate exists, this sends nothing. Requires Alternate Repeat support.

Normally send Escape. With Shift or Gui held, send the Grave key instead; Shift produces a tilde on a US host layout. Firmware settings can change which held modifiers select Grave.
Hold for left Shift; tap for an opening parenthesis. Space Cadet behavior depends on firmware settings. The default tap assumes a US host layout; firmware can customize the tap key and modifiers.
Hold for right Shift; tap for a closing parenthesis. Space Cadet behavior depends on firmware settings. The default tap assumes a US host layout; firmware can customize the tap key and modifiers.
Hold for left Ctrl; tap for an opening parenthesis. Space Cadet behavior depends on firmware settings. The default tap assumes a US host layout; firmware can customize the tap key and modifiers.
Hold for right Ctrl; tap for a closing parenthesis. Space Cadet behavior depends on firmware settings. The default tap assumes a US host layout; firmware can customize the tap key and modifiers.
Hold for left Alt; tap for an opening parenthesis. Space Cadet behavior depends on firmware settings. The default tap assumes a US host layout; firmware can customize the tap key and modifiers.
Hold for right Alt; tap for a closing parenthesis. Space Cadet behavior depends on firmware settings. The default tap assumes a US host layout; firmware can customize the tap key and modifiers.
Hold for right Shift; tap for Enter. Space Cadet behavior depends on firmware settings.

On press, toggle the lock on the highest active layer so it stays active after its momentary layer key is released. Press Layer Lock again on that layer, or press its MO/TT/LM key, to unlock it. Firmware can add an idle unlock timeout. Locking the base layer has no effect. The lock is runtime state, not a saved default layer. Requires Layer Lock support.

Hold to enable the lower Fn layer, plus the adjust layer when FN_MO23 is also held. Defaults are layers 1 and 3; firmware configuration can change them. Release to deactivate that Fn layer and update the combined adjust layer. Requires firmware Tri Layer support; these activations are not saved.

Hold to enable the upper Fn layer, plus the adjust layer when FN_MO13 is also held. Defaults are layers 2 and 3; firmware configuration can change them. Release to deactivate that Fn layer and update the combined adjust layer. Requires firmware Tri Layer support; these activations are not saved.

On release, start recording keyboard events into dynamic macro 1, replacing its previous recording. Stop with Stop Recording. The recording buffer has limited space and is lost when the keyboard restarts. This is separate from stored Vial macro slots. Requires Dynamic Macro support.

On release, start recording keyboard events into dynamic macro 2, replacing its previous recording. Stop with Stop Recording. The recording buffer has limited space and is lost when the keyboard restarts. This is separate from stored Vial macro slots. Requires Dynamic Macro support.

On press, finish the current dynamic macro recording. The result stays in temporary keyboard memory until restart and can be played with its Dynamic Macro Play key. It does not write a stored Vial macro slot. Requires Dynamic Macro support.

On release, replay the events recorded in dynamic macro 1. An empty recording sends nothing. Recordings live only in keyboard memory until restart and are separate from stored Vial macro slots. Requires Dynamic Macro support.

On release, replay the events recorded in dynamic macro 2. An empty recording sends nothing. Recordings live only in keyboard memory until restart and are separate from stored Vial macro slots. Requires Dynamic Macro support.

Send the special locking Caps Lock HID usage for a mechanically latching switch. This is different from the normal momentary Caps Lock key. Host support is limited and it is usually inappropriate for an ordinary key switch.

Send the special locking Num Lock HID usage for a mechanically latching switch. This is different from the normal momentary Num Lock key. Host support is limited and it is usually inappropriate for an ordinary key switch.

Send the special locking Scroll Lock HID usage for a mechanically latching switch. This is different from the normal momentary Scroll Lock key. Host support is limited and it is usually inappropriate for an ordinary key switch.

Use mouse-key speed preset 0 for pointer movement and scrolling. Normally hold it together with movement or wheel keys; constant-speed firmware may instead latch the preset after a tap. Firmware settings define its speed and whether selection is momentary. It does not move the pointer by itself or save a speed to EEPROM. Requires firmware Mouse Keys support.

Use mouse-key speed preset 1 for pointer movement and scrolling. Normally hold it together with movement or wheel keys; constant-speed firmware may instead latch the preset after a tap. Firmware settings define its speed and whether selection is momentary. It does not move the pointer by itself or save a speed to EEPROM. Requires firmware Mouse Keys support.

Use mouse-key speed preset 2 for pointer movement and scrolling. Normally hold it together with movement or wheel keys; constant-speed firmware may instead latch the preset after a tap. Firmware settings define its speed and whether selection is momentary. It does not move the pointer by itself or save a speed to EEPROM. Requires firmware Mouse Keys support.
Press to hold mouse button 4; release to release it. The host application or mouse-button mapping determines its action. Requires firmware Mouse Keys support.
Press to hold mouse button 5; release to release it. The host application or mouse-button mapping determines its action. Requires firmware Mouse Keys support.
Send the non-US hash key. The host keyboard layout determines the symbol.
Send the non-US backslash key. The host keyboard layout determines the symbol.
Send the JIS Ro key, commonly backslash or underscore. The host layout determines the symbol.
Send the JIS Katakana/Hiragana key. Behavior depends on the host input method.
Send the JIS Yen key. The host layout determines the symbol.
Send the JIS Henkan conversion key. Behavior depends on the host input method.
Send the JIS Muhenkan non-conversion key. Behavior depends on the host input method.
Send the language 1 key, used for Korean Hangul/English switching or Japanese Mac Kana. Behavior depends on the host layout.
Send the language 2 key, used for Korean Hanja or Japanese Mac Eisu. Behavior depends on the host layout.

Press to hold mouse button 1; release to release it. Tap for a click, or hold while moving the pointer to drag. Usually the primary or left button; host remapping can change the action. Requires firmware Mouse Keys support.

Press to hold mouse button 2; release to release it. Tap for a click, or hold while moving the pointer to drag. Usually the secondary or right button; host remapping can change the action. Requires firmware Mouse Keys support.

Press to hold mouse button 3; release to release it. Tap for a click, or hold while moving the pointer to drag. Usually the middle button; host remapping can change the action. Requires firmware Mouse Keys support.

Move the mouse pointer up while this key is held. Release stops the movement command; inertia-mode firmware can let the pointer glide afterward. Speed and acceleration depend on firmware Mouse Keys settings.
Send mouse-wheel scrolling up while held; release to stop. Scroll speed, acceleration and the host's natural-scrolling setting determine the result. Requires firmware Mouse Keys support.

Move the mouse pointer down while this key is held. Release stops the movement command; inertia-mode firmware can let the pointer glide afterward. Speed and acceleration depend on firmware Mouse Keys settings.
Send mouse-wheel scrolling down while held; release to stop. Scroll speed, acceleration and the host's natural-scrolling setting determine the result. Requires firmware Mouse Keys support.

Move the mouse pointer left while this key is held. Release stops the movement command; inertia-mode firmware can let the pointer glide afterward. Speed and acceleration depend on firmware Mouse Keys settings.
Send mouse-wheel scrolling left while held; release to stop. Scroll speed, acceleration and the host's natural-scrolling setting determine the result. Requires firmware Mouse Keys support.

Move the mouse pointer right while this key is held. Release stops the movement command; inertia-mode firmware can let the pointer glide afterward. Speed and acceleration depend on firmware Mouse Keys settings.
Send mouse-wheel scrolling right while held; release to stop. Scroll speed, acceleration and the host's natural-scrolling setting determine the result. Requires firmware Mouse Keys support.

Press to request that the host select the next media track. Holding may repeat or seek according to the host and media application. This controls host media, not the keyboard speaker.

Press to request that the host toggle media playback between playing and paused. Holding may repeat or seek according to the host and media application. This controls host media, not the keyboard speaker.
